piezo_force_times_d.repo: V = F x d14 = 500 N x 1.4 pC/N = 0.73 mV (04_THE_MASTER_COPY)
piezo_force_times_d.finding: F x d is a charge in coulombs, not a voltage, and 500 x 1.4e-12 = 7.0e-10, not 7.3e-4. A voltage needs a capacitance (V = Q/C), which the repo never states.

leap_hole_rule.repo: Skip/add one hole every 6 standstills (111.7 yr)
leap_hole_rule.verdict: SOUND as arithmetic: one hole slips every 6.25 revolutions, so "+1 hole per 6" keeps the marker within half a hole for over a millennium. The repo gives the drift as +0.049 yr; it is -0.053 yr.

altar_prediction_vs_lifetime.repo: Altar Stone holds 560 remanence layers at 18.6-yr spacing; 56 TL peaks at 18.6-yr periodicity
altar_prediction_vs_lifetime.verdict: SELF-CONTRADICTORY: 560 layers need 10,416 years and 56 peaks need 1,042 years, but the repo says the machine ran for 140 years (7.5 standstills).

yz_59_pits.verdict: ARITHMETIC TRUE, MEANING UNSUPPORTED: Z hole 8 may lie under stone 8 (count uncertain), and any count near 59 matches something.

acoustic_exclusion.repo: Builders at Durrington 2.5 km away excluded by a 5 dB acoustic shadow
acoustic_exclusion.verdict: Distance alone puts speech about 17 dB below the threshold of hearing, before any stones. The 5 dB "shadow" plays no role in excluding anyone 2.5 km away.

aubrey_code.repo: (56,3) cyclic code, generator g(x) = x^3+x+1, d_min = 18, corrects 8-hole bursts, "Reed-Solomon equivalent"
aubrey_code.verdict: WRONG: a degree-3 generator makes a (56,53) code, and since x^3+x+1 divides x^7+1 that code has weight-2 codewords (d = 2). Used as a check polynomial it gives a (56,3) code with d = 32. No version has d = 18. Reed-Solomon codes need symbols from a field with more than n elements, so a binary length-56 code cannot be one. And three moving markers are not codeword symbols anyway.

astronomy.verdict: At Stonehenge the two directions meet at 91.3 deg (simple geometry) to 93.4 deg (first gleam, refraction, parallax), not 90. An exact right angle falls at 49.9-50.7 N, south of Stonehenge. The angle changes 2.7 deg per degree of latitude, so a rectangle good to 0.5 deg fits a band ~41 km wide (4% of Britain's span). That is a loose coincidence, not "ONLY at 51.18 N +/-50 km".

sacred_rod_look_elsewhere.verdict: With 8 Earth lengths and round divisors, a random rod length in 0.5-2 m matches something this well far more often than 1 in 5,000, and the rod itself (Heath) is a reconstruction, not a measurement.
